Trace, implement and test: Bitwise Subsequence

Study exercise derived from this source. Explain the approach in your own words, work through an example, and identify edge cases. For code, implement your own version and discuss its time and space complexity.

Original source context
package DynamicProgramming;

import java.util.ArrayList;

public class BitwiseSubsequence {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        int[] arr = { 15, 6, 5, 12, 1 };
        helper(arr, arr.length, 0, new ArrayList<Integer>());
    }

    public static void helper(int[] arr, int n, int curr, ArrayList<Integer> sequence) {
        if (curr == n) {
            System.out.println(sequence);
            return;
        }
        sequence.add(arr[curr]);
        helper(arr, n, curr + 1, sequence);
        sequence.remove(sequence.size() - 1);
        helper(arr, n, curr + 1, sequence);
    }
}
